question: Should exact requester consumption count as terminal descendant delivery even when the requester's later outward send fails?
rationale: Source and tests can prove the mechanism, but they cannot decide whether consumption by an orchestrating requester satisfies OpenClaw's product-level delivery contract or whether descendant retry must continue until durable outward delivery.

options.title: Accept bounded consumption credit
options.body: Treat explicit, session-matched, run-window-matched requester consumption as terminal delivery after exact-head live restart and negative retry proof is supplied.

options.title: Require outward delivery
options.body: Keep descendants retryable until the requester result is durably delivered outward, even when the requester has already incorporated their output.

options.title: Fold into durable inbox work
options.body: Pause this implementation and resolve consumption, retry, restart, and outward-delivery semantics through the broader durable completion inbox tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/67777.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded consumption credit
recommendation.body: Treat explicit, session-matched, run-window-matched requester consumption as terminal delivery after exact-head live restart and negative retry proof is supplied.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest recent history signal across the central fallback, lifecycle, and persisted registry surfaces affected by this semantic choice.
